codeReview.summary: Implementation correctly adds ContextMenu and hover-reveal '...' DropdownMenu button to Inspirations, Videos, and Persons listing pages. All three pages follow the same visual and behavioral pattern: ContextMenu wrapper with matching menu items, hover-reveal MoreVertical button (Button variant='secondary' size='icon' className='size-7'), destructive styling on Delete, dialogManager.confirm() for delete confirmations, and query cache invalidation via respective *Keys.all. The InspirationCard and PersonCard were cleanly extracted as separate components. The VideoCard was minimally modified — only wrapped in ContextMenu and the handleDelete signature simplified (event parameter removed since propagation stopping is handled on the trigger button). All imports are correct and verified against source files. No regressions — tsc, eslint, and vitest all pass.

issues.description: PersonCard uses an inline type `{ id: string; name: string; description: string | null; images: string[] }` instead of importing the Person type from Prisma or inferring from the query return type. This works but is less maintainable — if the Person model changes, this inline type won't auto-update. The InspirationCard correctly uses the exported `InspirationListItem` type. Consider using the query's return type or the Prisma type for consistency.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The architecture.md library entry says 'Cards are rendered inline in the client component (not as separate feature components)'. This feature extracted InspirationCard and PersonCard as separate function components within the same file, which is a reasonable pattern but technically contradicts the documented convention. The documentation could be updated to say 'Cards are defined in the same file as the listing page client component, either inline or as extracted function components'.
